current.text: The Spurs starting lineup is not set. Harper, Fox, Castle and the forward spot (likely Tobias Harris) are all in the mix.
Tobias Harris has a calf strain.
The newest view is that Harper may start next to Castle and Fox. One expert is more and more convinced he will start and be the Spurs' second best player by the end of the season.
He shares a crowded backcourt with Fox and Castle. The team staggers its three guards so that at least two are always on the court, and more three-guard lineups are expected.
He could take on-ball time from Fox and Castle.
Experts expect about 28 to 29 minutes. Josh moved his line to 29, while Dan takes the under on 28.5.
Experts call his mock draft price of about 70 to 84 too high. One says he leaves no value at rank 79 and fits closer to 100, because the backcourt that limited his minutes is still there.
Experts doubt that his strong late-season shooting from last season will last. One host says he would be a top five player if it holds.
The Spurs want to win now and are projected near the top of the West, with one prediction of 63 wins. The roster is deep, so Coach Mitch Johnson has to balance a deep rotation.

durable.text: The Spurs see him as a future superstar and part of their long-term backcourt with Castle.
He is a much better defender than people think.
His category profile is balanced with no weak category. His best areas are FG% for a guard and assists.

note: Yahoo and ESPN both put his average cost near 4.5 USD (ranks 85 and 99), and he was not drafted in our league last season. Experts say his mock draft spot of about 70 to 84 is too high, but at about 5 USD he is a fair late buy. With no weak category and good FG% for a guard plus assists, he fits any build. Early in the season, check whether he starts while Tobias Harris has a calf strain, whether he gets close to 29 minutes, and whether last season's late shooting holds.
